\newcommand{\vsixEFourBSentence}{In E4b (152 predeclared trials; every kill was confirmed to land with its request outstanding), the post-stop count is read from the sink's database. The sink's ordering check found 0 violations. In 10 trials (exit after commit in complete) the harness log counted a post-stop commit that the database shows was made before the stop, which is why E4b counts from the database.}

\newcommand{\vsixEFourIdentitySentence}{The counts reconcile trial by trial: in 144 of 144 fault-free halting and revoking trials, the effects committed after enforcement equal the calls in flight at enforcement plus those emitted but not yet accepted, less those refused, and in 72 of 72 fence trials none committed and every call in flight was discarded. The decision always falls just after the agent emits a burst of 4 calls (the 20\,s warm-up is a whole number of 2\,s steps). With the stop enforced at once, a halt lets that burst through and a revocation refuses it, which is most of the difference between the two in the drawn cell; with any delay the burst is admitted before the stop takes effect, and the median counts after enforcement for halting and revoking were 10 and 9 at \(L = 1\)\,s; 12 and 12 at \(L = 5\)\,s; 13 and 14 at \(L = 35\)\,s. \newcommand{\vsixESixBSentence}{Under one classification rule, E6's PostgreSQL 16 trigger is a writer-supplied condition, not sink-enforced as E6 labelled it: a stale write that leaves out the epoch field committed in 40 of 40 runs. Every executed surface has a mechanism that the surface itself enforces: PostgreSQL 16 REVOKE writer role, etcd v3.5.17 RBAC revoke, and POSIX filesystem directory mode bits. Enforcement by the surface is necessary for a fence, not sufficient; the next two properties decide whether the mechanism is one. Among working fences, a stale writer claiming the new epoch was refused in every run only where the epoch is carried by a credential (PostgreSQL 16 REVOKE writer role and etcd v3.5.17 RBAC revoke); where it is carried by the address and the request, the claim was accepted in every run. With PostgreSQL 16 REVOKE writer role, stale effects were ordered after the fence in 20 of 20 races (249 effects in all), and none of those races had a stale write that started after the acknowledgement: it stops statements not yet started, not ones already running, which is revocation at the broker rather than a fence at the sink. E6's race, repeated 20 times without added load, starved the PostgreSQL 16 trigger fence in 18 of 20 (95\% CI 0.68--0.99) and the table-lock variant in 0 of 20; under added load the counts were 13 and 0.}

The crash-surviving hold (P3) passed on PostgreSQL 16 and etcd v3.5.17 and had no mechanism on POSIX filesystem. E6's P3 ruling excluded a filesystem design built on staged files and rename while counting etcd's lease-staged key, whose promotion also depends on a compare the promoter supplies; we report this inconsistency rather than reclassify after the fact.}
